# Funded awards and program contacts for skin pigment measurement (external report, 2026-11-28)

> **Origin:** report from an outside AI deep-research tool (Google Gemini), written from a prompt the project coordinator gave the project owner; pasted by the owner into the project thread on 2026-11-28 at 02:35 UTC. The prompt asked for funded NIH RePORTER and SBIR.gov awards from 2015 onward on objective skin pigmentation or colour measurement, imaging tools for pigmentary disorders, melanocyte transplantation, and vitiligo or hypopigmentation devices, plus NIAMS and NIBIB program officers covering skin imaging.
> **Status: leads only, planning only.** Nothing here is evidence for the ledger. The pasted text lost its hyperlinks; the words "NIH RePORTER", "SBIR.gov" and the link labels are as received. Saved verbatim below the line (tab-separated tables kept as tabs); only this header and the check appendix at the end were added. Nobody named here has been contacted.

NIAMS and NIBIB Program Officers and Program Areas Covering Skin Imaging

NIAMS (National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases)

⚬ Skin Repair, Pigmentation and Appendages, Vasculature/Lymphatic Systems Program — Covers pigmentation, wound healing, and skin appendages within NIAMS's Skin Biology and Diseases portfolio (alongside the Epidermis, Dermis and Skin Senses Program and the Skin Immunology and Diseases, Skin Microbiome Program).
  ⚬ Program Director: Alexey Belkin, Ph.D. (alexey.belkin@nih.gov, 301-827-6475) — listed as NIAMS inquiry contact on NIH Guide Notice NOT-AR-23-019 and identified as Director for the Skin Repair, Pigmentation, and Appendages Program in the Skin of Color Society Summit Program.
  ⚬ Program Area Links: NIH Almanac – NIAMS Supported Scientific Programs | NIH Grants – NIAMS Research Fit & Interest Areas
⚬ NIAMS Small Business (SBIR/STTR) Program — Explicitly includes "Research and development of new biomarkers or novel imaging technologies for arthritis, musculoskeletal and skin diseases" and autoimmune skin diseases including vitiligo.
  ⚬ Program Contact: NIAMS_SBIR_STTR@nih.gov (page also lists primary contact Dr. Isaah Vincent, isaah.vincent@nih.gov, 301-496-0747).
  ⚬ Link: NIH Grants – NIAMS Small Business Interest Areas
⚬ Note: A standalone NIAMS program officer specifically titled for skin imaging (separate from the Skin Biology/Pigmentation and SBIR/STTR contacts above) was not found in the retrieved results.

NIBIB (National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering)

NIBIB organizes its extramural portfolio by imaging modality and engineering discipline rather than by organ system; optical skin imaging and spectroscopy projects align primarily with its biophotonics/optical imaging portfolio.

⚬ Optical Imaging and Spectroscopy Program — Covers biophotonics, biomedical optical imaging, and spectroscopy technologies.
  ⚬ Program Director: Afrouz Azari Anderson, Ph.D. (afrouz.anderson@nih.gov, 301-496-4558) — oversees biophotonics research activities and manages the Optical Imaging and Spectroscopy portfolio.
  ⚬ Link: NIH Research – Afrouz Azari Anderson, Ph.D.
⚬ National Centers for Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering (P41) & Optical Imaging / Informatics Leadership
  ⚬ Program / Division Director: Behrouz Shabestari, Ph.D. — Director, National Centers for Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, and Division Director, Division of Health Informatics Technologies; his NIH profile notes direction of NIBIB programs in Optical Imaging and Spectroscopy and involvement across R01, R21, R21/R33, SBIR/STTR, and P41 mechanisms.
  ⚬ Link: NIH Research – Behrouz Shabestari, Ph.D.
⚬ Note: Additional modality-specific NIBIB program officer pages (for example, photoacoustic/ultrasound imaging or dedicated NIBIB SBIR/STTR contacts) were not found in the retrieved results.

## Check against the public record (added 2026-11-28, this project; not part of the report)

Checked from the cloud environment on 2026-11-28, 02:36 to 02:45 UTC. Each award was looked up by its grant number, not by title. Sources:

- **NIH RePORTER API** (`POST https://api.reporter.nih.gov/v2/projects/search`, criteria `project_nums` = the grant number, or `appl_ids` for 9718091). The public page for each record is `https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/<appl_id>`; the appl_id is in the table.
- **SBIR.gov.** The search pages and the awards API (`https://www.sbir.gov/awards?keywords=Hydrostasis`, `https://api.www.sbir.gov/public/api/awards?firm=Hydrostasis`, `https://www.sbir.gov/api/awards.json?firm=Hydrostasis`) all returned HTTP 403 to the cloud environment. SBIR.gov's own bulk award file (`https://data.www.sbir.gov/awarddatapublic/award_data.csv`, 207,731 rows, last modified 2026-01-01) was reachable and was read in full; the matching rows were kept. No per-award SBIR.gov page link is given, because none was opened.
- **NIH staff and program pages:** grants.nih.gov NOT-AR-23-019; grants.nih.gov "Find a fit" page for NIAMS (`https://www.grants.nih.gov/funding/find-a-fit-for-your-research/nih-institutes-centers-offices/NIAMS`); nibib.nih.gov staff pages for Afrouz Azari Anderson and Behrouz Shabestari and the program page `https://www.nibib.nih.gov/research-funding/optical-imaging-spectroscopy`. Every niams.nih.gov page tried returned HTTP 403 (staff directory `/about/directory/alexey-belkin`, `/grants-funding/supported-scientific-areas/skin-repair-pigmentation-and-appendages`, `/grants-funding/funding-policies-guidelines/small-business-research`), as did `seed.nih.gov/NIAMS_SBIR_home` and the NIH Almanac NIAMS page.

Saved copies (project files folder, not committed): `external-reports/funded-awards/reporter_<grant number>.json` (raw API answers), `sbir_gov_bulk_matched_rows.csv` (the 5 matching SBIR.gov rows, contact columns dropped), `pages/*.txt` (plain text of the NIH pages read, and of the 2024 Skin of Color Society symposium program).

Marks: **VERIFIED** (the record exists and every field the report gives matches), **VERIFIED, with differences** (the record exists; one field is wrong, missing or loosely worded, named in the last column), **DOES NOT MATCH** (the record contradicts the report's claim), **NOT CHECKABLE** (the record could not be reached; exact query given).

## What the verified rows mean for a grant route (this project's reading, 2026-11-28; judgment, not funding advice)

The project's grant idea is an objective colour measurement tool for small white spots, through a small company with a university partner (SBIR or STTR). Using only the rows marked VERIFIED:

1. **Nobody in these records funds what this project would build.** Every funded pigment measurement in the list (A1 to A4, A6) measures skin colour to correct a pulse oximeter or another sensor, not to judge a pigment disorder. The skin imaging awards (A5, A7, A8) target cancer, moles or inflammation. The vitiligo small business awards (A10 to A12) are all drugs. That is a gap, which helps a novelty argument, but it also means there is no funded precedent to point a reviewer to.
2. **The written fit is at NIAMS.** NIAMS names "novel imaging technologies for ... skin diseases" as an approved small business topic, even above the usual budget limit, and names vitiligo as a skin disease it supports. IGH is not named. An application would have to argue the tool for pigment loss in general (vitiligo and IGH), not IGH alone.
3. **NIAMS small business grants do not take clinical trials.** A study that only photographs and measures spots is probably not a clinical trial under NIH's definition, but a study that treats spots and then measures them may be. The first grant would need to be measurement validation only. That fits the current plan; it would need checking against NIH's clinical trial definition before writing.
4. **The STTR pattern with a university partner is real and recent.** A8 (Lumo Imaging with Johns Hopkins, NIBIB, $252,388) and A12 (MC1R Ventures with University of Cincinnati, NIAMS, $295,913) are Phase I STTRs of the size PR 20 already reported. Lumo also won an NSF STTR Phase I the year before, so the NSF and NIH routes can run side by side for the same device.
5. **Who would read it.** On the NIAMS side, Alexey Belkin is the program officer on 30 current NIAMS pigment and melanocyte projects, so he is the likely contact, though his title could not be confirmed from here. On the NIBIB side, Afrouz Azari Anderson runs Optical Imaging and Spectroscopy, which states an emphasis on cheap, portable, non-invasive devices, and a colour-calibrated camera fits that wording. Do not use Isaah Vincent as a small business contact. None of these people has been contacted, and nobody should be without the project owner's go-ahead.
